thesis: RLI Corp (NYSE: RLI) writes specialty casualty, property and surety insurance. Q3 2026 10-Q (full text downloaded; income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, segment tables, reserve development, debt and capital sections read) filed 2026-10-21; 8-K 2026-11-09 is a director retirement only; earnings release exhibit not read. Nine month gross premiums written 1,605.8M (+3%), net premiums earned 1,253.4M (+3.8%); casualty NPE up on commercial excess and personal umbrella (+19%). Combined ratio 85.9% versus 84.0% (casualty 98.7%, property 59.6%, surety 86.9%). Underwriting income 176.5M (193.3M). Net investment income 135.1M (+15%). Net earnings 303.9M versus 312.2M for nine months and 81.0M versus 124.6M in Q3 (unrealized equity gains -3.3M versus +42.0M; realized gains 8.6M versus 18.3M). TTM net earnings 395.1M (FY2025 403.3M less 312.2M plus 303.9M). Shares 91,732,032 (2026-09-30 and 2026-10-14 cover); price 68.70 (NYSE close 2026-11-11, two publishers); market cap about 6.30B; about 15.9x TTM earnings. Shareholders equity 1,696.2M (total assets 6,445.6M less liabilities 4,749.4M), so 3.7x book; nine month return on average equity about 17.5% (about 23% annualized). Equity fell from 1,778.2M despite earnings because of a 2.00 special dividend and 145.5M other comprehensive loss (117.8M in Q3). Debt 297.0M (5.375% notes due 2036 issued 2026-03-03; 100M short-term debt repaid), about 15% of capital. Favorable prior-year reserve development 98M in nine months (74M a year earlier). Nine month OCF 382.7M (457.5M); capex 6.2M. Repurchases 18M under the 250M plan authorized 2026-05-14. Investments and cash 4.91B.
counterthesis: Reserve releases of 98M equal about 7.8 points of net premiums earned, so the combined ratio excluding releases is about 93.7%; casualty at 98.7% includes 36M of releases, so underlying casualty (the growing segment) is above 100%. Premium growth is only 3% and the property segment's 59.6% ratio looks like a benign catastrophe year that will not persist. At 3.7x book and 15.9x earnings the price already pays for a premium return; a normalized catastrophe year and lower releases would cut earnings substantially. Q3 net earnings fell 35% and OCF fell 16%. Excess casualty and umbrella lines carry social inflation and long-tail reserve risk (unpaid losses 3.0B, 1.8x equity). Equity is sensitive to interest rates (OCI -145M in nine months). The 3.96% headline yield includes the 2.00 special dividend (inferred: regular dividend about 0.72), so the regular yield is about 1%. Peers (Kinsale, Palomar, Markel, W.R. Berkley) were not compared and I did not establish why the stock is flat since 2026-11-05.
invalidation: Reserve development turning adverse, combined ratio ex-releases above 100% in casualty with no pricing offset, net premiums earned growth below inflation, equity falling again because of rates, or a large catastrophe loss year. Supportive: stable combined ratio below 90% with premium growth above 5%.
